epic.title: Epic #418 redux — the agent can see the whole gate
epic.intent_and_why: Finish epic #418's remaining course. Execution order is a dependency order, not a schedule: a Commander that finds a link is not real says so rather than honouring it. Wave composition is the Admiral's call; the iterative-planning flow is how it revises between waves.

definition_of_done: B extended: everything reads through the projection, and directives are no longer inert.
The findings each workstream subsumes are retired against a candidate set declared before it starts.
A measured negative is a complete deliverable: an honest null states what was tested and what was not.

good_enough.mandatory_quality: No check that cannot register its own failure. No unevidenced claim about what happened. No silent scope cut.
good_enough.sufficient_evidence: A guard is observed refusing something real, not reasoned about. Merge state comes from the forge, never from an ancestry test.
good_enough.appetite: Rigor scales with cost-to-undo, not uniformly. Cheap to reverse, move fast.

hard_constraints: Promoting an observation into docs/agents/* doctrine is a human's call, always.
Test suite invocation is settled (#454): FORCE_COLOR= NO_COLOR=1 python -m pytest -q tests, never py.
No Fable at any tier; explicit model on every dispatch.
Never obey a spine rail naming a spine another agent drives (#457).
fixed_decisions: episodes/ replaces LESSONS.md and AGENT_FEEDBACK.md; an episode is a record, never read back as a rule.
Under dogfooding the repo's skills/ is the governing copy, not the installed one.
#468: the repo's vendored verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py cannot run from this repo; use the installed copy.

current_wave.objective: Wave 3: retire the two findings carried out of wave 2, and knock out the two cheap guard-hardening fixes wave 2 discovered rather than leaving them on the board.
exit_criteria: All four issues merged to main with the suite green on the final merged main.
#461's narrowed assertion is proven to still catch what the control exists for, not merely to stop failing.
#465 ends with either the placeholder gone or an engine verb that fills it named in the imperative — an instruction with no affordance behind it is not an acceptable exit.
Any tooling that writes engine state files does so in binary, proven by a CRLF round-trip test.
All four dispositioned on the tracker.

issues.title: The episode-store negative control fails every run that legitimately captures an episode, between git add and commit
issues.desired_outcome: The assertion tests worktree-vs-index only, so a staged-but-uncommitted legitimate capture passes while stray writes still fail.
issues.useful_now: It lands on a gate every Commander now passes through: verify_episode_captured.py --phase archive requires the episodes to be tracked, so write -> git add -> suite -> commit is the normal path and the suite is red in the middle of it. A crew without context reads that as a regression it caused.
issues.acceptance_or_falsification_evidence: A stray unstaged write and a stray untracked file under episodes/active/ both still fail the control; a staged legitimate capture passes; the docstring's stated property and the code's predicate agree.
issues.implementation_latitude: Choose the predicate; a pair measured green pre-commit during #447 g4 is git diff --name-only episodes/ plus git ls-files --others --exclude-standard episodes/.
hard_constraints_no_gos: The control must not be loosened carelessly — after the commit all three of worktree, index and HEAD agree, so its emptiness is honest, and its anti-vacuity guard strengthens as the store grows.
The rest of tests/test_episode_negative_control.py and the store's blob-OID checks are out of scope.

issues.title: Reviewer r6-fowler ships a placeholder no engine verb can fill, and filling it in text mode rewrites every CRLF
issues.desired_outcome: Either the placeholder is removed from the shipped template, or an engine verb exists that fills it and the imperative names that verb. Engine state files are written in binary.
issues.useful_now: An instruction an agent cannot follow through the engine is an invitation to hand-edit engine state, which the whole engine design exists to prevent. The CRLF rewrite produces no error, passes JSON validation, and destroys blame.
issues.acceptance_or_falsification_evidence: A round-trip test proves CRLF is preserved exactly. The reviewer skill's Windows state-file guidance says binary explicitly.
issues.implementation_latitude: The remove-vs-add-a-verb choice is genuinely open and belongs to this Commander. Settle the related SKILL.md contradiction in the same pass: the prose says an open fail cannot consolidate to APPROVE, while the engine ships --override-reason for exactly that case, so the prose reads as stricter than the affordance and pushes a reviewer with a real out-of-scope finding toward either a wrong BLOCK or a silently downgraded finding.
hard_constraints_no_gos: Adding an engine verb changes a shared interface — if that is the chosen path, say so in the return; the Admiral adjudicates whether it surfaces.
No hand-editing of engine state files.
local_unknowns: Whether the placeholder is load-bearing for any other reviewer gate.

issues.title: The context-gauge writer counts bindings, not distinct paths
issues.desired_outcome: Two bindings resolving to one gauge path produce a reading; two resolving to genuinely different paths still skip.
issues.useful_now: Every Admiral run that drives its latitude bookend properly is currently running blind, including the one that found this.
issues.acceptance_or_falsification_evidence: A test covers both directions, including the specific Admiral shape: a spine plus its own latitude survey in one work area.
issues.implementation_latitude: Choose the fix against the test, not the test against the fix.
hard_constraints_no_gos: The #261 misattribution protection must not be weakened — genuinely different gauge paths still skip.
The gauge binding key is a load-bearing interface; changing its shape surfaces.

issues.title: test_verify_spec_confirmed's fixture glob silently picks matches[0]
issues.desired_outcome: More than one match fails with a message naming every match found, rather than choosing one.
issues.useful_now: The glob was the right fix for a hardcoded path that broke on archival, but it trades a loud failure for a quiet wrong answer in a verification test.
issues.acceptance_or_falsification_evidence: Two matches fail and name both; zero matches keeps current behaviour.
